sections.html:
McClain County is in central Oklahoma, about 580 square miles of land and water, with Purcell as the county seat. Cleveland County and part of Pottawatomie County lie to the north, Pontotoc to the east, Garvin to the south and Grady to the west, per the Oklahoma Historical Society.

The South Canadian River forms the northern border, and the Washita River flows near the southwestern corner. The west is hilly and was once covered in blackjack oak, while the southeastern arm is level lowland. Incorporated towns, as of 2010, were Blanchard, Byars, Cole, Dibble, Goldsby, Newcastle, Rosedale, Washington, Wayne and Purcell.

sections.h2: What does the McClain County Clerk do?
sections.html:
The McClain County Clerk is the registrar of deeds for the county and is one of eight elected officials. The clerk's page lists deeds, mortgages, plats, mineral interests, liens, court judgments, tax liens, oil and gas leases, powers of attorney and trust agreements among the records kept.

The office is at 121 North 2nd Avenue in Purcell, with a mailing address of PO Box 629, Purcell, OK 73080. Land records can be reached at 405-527-3360, and hours are 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM. The clerk also serves as secretary to the Board of County Commissioners, the Excise Board, the Tax Roll Correction Board and the Equalization Board.

Military discharge records on a DD-214 are recorded free for veterans.

sections.h2: What does recording a deed cost in McClain County?
sections.html:
The standard rate is $18.00 for the first page, which includes $8.00 for recording and $10.00 for preservation, plus $2.00 for each added page. A document that misses the statutory format rules costs more.

ItemFee
First page, standard$18.00
Each additional page$2.00
First page, non-conforming$25.00 plus $10.00 preservation
Each additional page, non-conforming$10.00
Plat of one block or less$10.00
Plat of more than one block$25.00
Certifying a copy, per page$1.00
Mechanics or materialmen's lien$10.00

The fee table cites 28 O.S. 32, and nonconforming documents are tied to subsection C of 19 O.S. 298. Mortgage recording and re-filing may involve fees payable to the County Treasurer, so call that office if you are recording a mortgage.

sections.h2: How is documentary stamp tax calculated in McClain County?
sections.html:
The clerk applies $0.75 for each $500 of the purchase price, rounding up to the next $500, and it applies only when the price exceeds $100. The county site has a calculator that does the rounding for you.

Proof of price must come with the deed. A closing statement, a notarized bill of sale or an affidavit of purchase price all work, and the clerk uses them only to compute the tax. They are not recorded. If the transfer is exempt, the exemption has to appear on the face of the deed.

  • $100,000 sale: 200 units of $500, so $150.
  • $233,900 sale, the Census Bureau median home value: 468 units, so $351.
  • Under 68 O.S. 3201, the tax is limited to conveyances of realty that are sold.

sections.h2: How far back do McClain County land records go?
sections.html:
The OKCountyRecords index for McClain County shows data and scanned images from January 1980, with new records added in real time. The clerk's page says the office preserves property records dating back to the original U.S. land grants, so older records are held in the office even though the online index starts later.

Searches online can be run by name, book and page, instrument type, recording dates and legal description, including quarter, section, township and range. That is useful on rural McClain County land, where a deed may describe a quarter section instead of a lot and block.

Fees apply for printed copies on the online site, and the revenue goes to support the county. For a sale, pull the last vesting deed and any open mortgage releases before you list, so gaps in the chain show up early.

sections.h2: How did McClain County get its shape and history?
sections.html:
McClain County was created at statehood in 1907 and named for Charles M. McClain, who sat in the 1906 Constitutional Convention. Before then, the area was part of the Chickasaw Nation's Pontotoc County and had few settlers.

Railroads built the towns. The Southern Kansas Railway and the Gulf, Colorado and Santa Fe met at Purcell in 1886 and 1887, and the Oklahoma Central Railway of 1906 established Washington, Cole and Blanchard. Purcell was a starting point for the Land Run of 1889. The Purcell site notes it was founded in 1887 as a railroad town and is called the Quarter Horse Capital of the World.

Ranching came first, tied to Montford Johnson and others, and the county still ran about 50,000 head of cattle in 2000. Farming added corn, cotton, alfalfa and wheat over time.

sections.h2: What do McClain County numbers say about local housing?
sections.html:
The 2019 to 2023 Census Bureau survey counts 43,779 people and 17,125 housing units in McClain County. The median home value is $233,900, and median household income is $84,778.

People43,779
Housing units17,125

Median household income$84,778
Owner-occupied78%

The state encyclopedia says the county's closeness to Oklahoma City and Norman has drawn commuters, and population rose from 27,740 in 2000 to 34,506 in 2010 and 41,667 in 2020. Interstate 35, Interstate 44 (the H. E. Bailey Turnpike, which ends in the county), and U.S. 62 and 77 cross the county. The Newcastle Bridge over the Canadian River, finished in 1913, gave county residents a direct route toward Oklahoma City.

sections.h2: What should McClain County sellers prepare before recording a deed?
sections.html:
Gather the signed and notarized deed, a closing statement or affidavit of purchase price, and a clear legal description. Then check the format, since a non-conforming page adds cost.

  1. Match the legal description to the last recorded deed.
  2. Prepare proof of the purchase price for the stamp tax.
  3. Check for any exemption and write it on the deed.
  4. Deliver the deed to 121 North 2nd Avenue in Purcell, or ask your title company to do so.
  5. Request a tax balance from the McClain County Treasurer, at 405-527-3261.

The treasurer's site says special assessments such as sewer, water, weed, cleaning, paving and nuisance abatement charges are certified to the treasurer after they become delinquent and are placed as a lien on the real estate account. The page we reviewed did not list due dates, so ask the office what applies to your account.

sections.h2: What do sellers in McClain County usually deal with?
sections.html:
Sellers in McClain County tend to hold either a commuter-town house near the Canadian River crossing or a rural tract with acreage. The stamp tax grows with the price, though the rate stays the same.

  • Inherited property where heirs live away from Purcell.
  • Land with mineral interests, which the clerk records separately.
  • Houses with lien or assessment questions.
  • Deeds that failed the format test and need to be redone.
